```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
```

# Question 1
```{r}
subway =
  read_csv("data/NYC_Transit_Subway_Entrance_And_Exit_Data.csv") |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  select(
    line, station_name, station_latitude, station_longitude,
    route1:route11,
    entry, vending, entrance_type, ada)
subway

subway =
  subway |>
  mutate(
    entry = ifelse(entry == "YES", TRUE, FALSE))
subway

# Could also use case_match
# mutate(
#  entry = case_match(
#    entry,
#    "YES" ~ TRUE,
#    "NO" ~ FALSE
# ))
```
After cleaning, there are 1868 observations and 19 variables in the dataset. The dataset contains information about subway lines, station names, station locations (latitude and longitude), routes served, whether entrances allow entry, vending availability, entrance types, and ADA compliance. For the data cleaning steps, I first imported the dataset using read_csv() and cleaned all variable names using clean_names(). The original dataset contained 32 variables in total, so I used select() to retain only the required variables and saved the cleaned dataset as subway. I then checked the dataset to make sure that it satisfied the requirements. Next I used mutate() to modify the existing entry variable. I am more familiar with ifelse(), it means if the observation equals to YES, then convert it to TURE. If else other than YES, then convert it to FALSE. I viewed the subway dataset again to check the result. The resulting dataset is not tidy because route information is stored across multiple variables (route1 through route11) instead of having route number and route name as distinct variables.

```{r}
subway |>
  distinct(line, station_name)
```
There are 465 distinct stations.

```{r}
subway |>
  filter(ada == TRUE) |>
  count(line, station_name)
```
Only 84 stations are ADA compliant.

```{r}
no_vending_entry =
  subway |>
  filter(vending == "NO", entry == TRUE)

no_vending =
  subway |>
  filter(vending == "NO")

nrow(no_vending_entry) / nrow(no_vending)
```
The proportion of station entrances / exits without vending allow entrance is 0.3770.

```{r}
# Reformat can't be proceeded, cuz the variable type of routes doesn't match. So fix the variable types first
str(subway)
subway =
  subway |>
  mutate(
    route8 = as.character(route8),
    route9 = as.character(route9),
    route10 = as.character(route10),
    route11 = as.character(route11)
  )
str(subway)

subway_reform =
  subway |>
  pivot_longer(route1:route11,
    names_to = "route_number",
    values_to = "route_name")
subway_reform

A_train =
  subway_reform |>
  filter(route_name == "A") |>
  distinct(line, station_name)
A_train

A_train_ada =
  subway_reform |>
  filter(route_name == "A", ada == TRUE) |>
  distinct(line, station_name)
A_train_ada
```
60 distinct stations serve the A train. Of those stations that serve the A train, only 17 are ADA compliant.


# Question 2
```{r}
trash =
  read_excel("data/202610 Trash Wheel Collection Data.xlsx",
    sheet = "Mr. Trash Wheel",
    range = "A2:N742"
  )
trash

trash =
  trash |>
  janitor::clean_names()
names(trash)

trash =
  trash |>
  mutate(
    sports_balls = round(sports_balls),
    sports_balls = as.integer(sports_balls)
  )
trash

str(trash)
```

```{r}
professor =
  read_excel("data/202610 Trash Wheel Collection Data.xlsx",
    sheet = "Professor Trash Wheel",
    range = "A2:M139"
  )
professor

professor =
  professor |>
  janitor::clean_names()
names(professor)

str(professor)
```

```{r}
gwynnda =
  read_excel("data/202610 Trash Wheel Collection Data.xlsx",
    sheet = "Gwynnda the Good Wheel of the W",
    range = "A2:L394"
  )
gwynnda

gwynnda =
  gwynnda |>
  janitor::clean_names()
names(gwynnda)

str(gwynnda)
```

```{r}
trash =
  trash |>
  mutate(
    trash_wheel = "Mr. Trash Wheel"
  )

professor =
  professor |>
  mutate(
    trash_wheel = "Professor Trash Wheel"
  )

gwynnda =
  gwynnda |>
  mutate(
    trash_wheel = "Gwynnda"
  )

# Combination can't be proceeded, cuz year and plastic_bottles have two different variable types (chr&dbl), so need to fix them first
trash =
  trash |>
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(year)
  )

professor |>
  filter(plastic_bottles == "dive")

professor =
  professor |>
  mutate(
    plastic_bottles = ifelse(plastic_bottles == "dive", NA, plastic_bottles),
    plastic_bottles = as.numeric(plastic_bottles)
  )
professor

trash_combined =
  bind_rows(trash, professor, gwynnda)
trash_combined
```
The merged dataset contains 1,269 observations and 15 variables. It tells key information including the name of the garbage truck, the trash can number, the month, year, and date of collection, as well as the weight and volume of the collected trash. The dataset also provides the specific types of trash collected, such as plastic bottles, cigarette butts, plastic bags, and wrapping paper.

```{r}
professor_total =
  trash_combined |>
  filter(trash_wheel == "Professor Trash Wheel")

professor_total |>
  summarize(
    total_weight = sum(weight_tons)
  )
```
The total weight of trash collected by Professor Trash Wheel was 295 tons.

```{r}
gwynnda_june_total =
  trash_combined |>
  filter(
    trash_wheel == "Gwynnda",
    year == 2022,
    month == "June"
  )

gwynnda_june_total |>
  summarize(
    total_cigarette_butts = sum(cigarette_butts)
  )
```
The total number of cigarette butts collected by Gwynnda in June 2022 was 18,120.
